newsitem.title: JAPAN: Aging Japan's economy to slow between 2011-2025.
newsitem.headline: Aging Japan's economy to slow between 2011-2025.

text.p: Japan's once mighty economy will slow from about the year 2011 as its population ages rapidly, with gross domestic product growth at an annual 0.8 to 1.7 percent, the Kyodo news agency reported on Saturday.
The projected figures for 2011-2025 will appear in a report the Ministry of International Trade and Industry (MITI) will issue by December, Kyodo quoted ministry sources as saying.
The report, the first of its kind on the economic outlook up to 2025, will urge steps to cope with the drawbacks of an aging society, Kyodo said.
MITI expects the economy to grow an average 3.1 percent from 1996 to 2000, and an average 1.9 to 2.4 percent from 2001 to 2010, Kyodo said.
Then it will further slow to 0.8 to 1.7 percent because an increase in the elderly coupled with a declining birth rate will leave a smaller work force.
Heavier pension contributions and a decrease in savings will overshadow Japan's future economy, the sources told Kyodo.
"An economic slowdown cannot be avoided unless we make the social welfare system more efficient and the labour market more flexible," MITI sources told Kyodo.
In the report, the ministry will propose promoting employment of elderly people and more women.
The report will suggest scrapping barriers between banking and securities firms and to allow the establishment of holding companies to pump strength into businesses.
Other proposals include a revamping of the medical insurance system to promote efficiency, and a drastic tax overhaul to reduce the tax burdens on companies.
Such measures would increase employment among the elderly and women of all ages, preventing a decline in the overall work force, the report says.
